<details>
<summary>Text description of this diagram</summary>

**Four phase headers across the top**, matching [section 4](/guidance/04-analytical-lifecycle/index.qmd):
engagement and scoping, design, analysis, delivery and sign-off.

**A green band beneath them: the analytical project record**, which runs across all four phases. One
place for everything about a piece of analysis, opened at scoping and added to as you go rather than
written at the end. How much of it you complete depends on your level, and keeping it proportionate
is the point. [GovS 010 section 6.7] Its nine sections are: 1. header, with title, reference, level,
analyst, commissioner, dates and the Business Critical answer; 2. the question, with the decision it
supports, the question, what is out of scope and the deadline; 3. data, with source, owner, extract
date, known quality issues, effect and access basis; 4. method, with the approach, why this and not
the alternatives, and tools and code repository; 5. assumptions, with the assumption, rationale,
impact if wrong, whether sensitivity was tested and who agreed it; 6. uncertainty, with principal
sources, how quantified or why not, and how communicated; 7. the decision log, including deviations
from the plan; 8. assurance and sign-off, with role, name, date and what they confirmed; 9. lessons
learned. **Level 1 completes sections 1, 2, 4 and 5 only**, which is realistically one side of A4.

**Then four templates, each created in one phase.**

- **Assurance level decision sheet**, phase 1, described in
  [section 5](/guidance/05-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd). Scoring impact and likelihood to reach
  your level, and the Business Critical test. Completed with your commissioner and attached to the
  specification. Rescored later only if the level changes, with the reason recorded.
- **Quality assurance checklist**, phase 2, described in
  [section 6](/guidance/06-doing-the-work/index.qmd). The checks required at your assurance level, planned
  here so the assurer's time is in the schedule. At Level 2 and above the reviewer is named before
  the work starts.
- **Quality assurance log**, phase 3, described in
  [section 6](/guidance/06-doing-the-work/index.qmd). The checks recorded as you do them, with what you
  found rather than only that you looked. A checklist shows somebody knew what to do; a log shows
  they did it.
- **Quality assurance statement**, phase 4, described in
  [section 9](/guidance/09-communicating-analysis/index.qmd). What was done and what the limits are:
  assumptions, uncertainty, limitations, and what the results can and cannot be used for. Published
  with the output at Level 3.

**Then where it ends up.** *Archived together, and linked from the output*: from Level 2, the
project record, the quality assurance log and the code are archived together and linked from the
output, because an artefact nobody can find from the output is an artefact nobody will look at.
*Register updated, review date set*: at Level 3 the register is updated and a review date is set, and
at Level 4 BCA the Business Critical register entry was made back at scoping, with
[section 8](/guidance/08-business-critical/index.qmd) carrying the rest. *The review record, kept with the
project record*: after release, [section 11](/guidance/11-review-and-continuous-improvement/index.qmd),
because a review filed separately from the analysis it reviews is a record nobody finds when the
analysis is next reused.

**And where NHSBSA analysis is published, once it is out.** Official statistics at the statistical
collections. Research and insight at data science projects. Open datasets at the Open Data Portal.
Analytical code at the code repositories.

**Created in place, not downloaded.** A template created in place is versioned and can be linked
from the output. One downloaded, filled in and saved somewhere is a template nobody can find
afterwards. The field lists are the part this playbook owns, so take them wherever your team works.
Records should be version controlled, securely stored and retrievable. [GovS 010 section 6.7]

**Where the templates are.** They are held on the NHSBSA SharePoint, alongside the rest of the
analytical documentation, and opening them needs NHSBSA network access. If you cannot reach them,
ask the Data Science, Advanced Analytics and Statistics team.

</details>
